The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran considers the issuance of unjust sentences against a group of Bahraini clerics and citizens on spurious pretexts to be a systematic and widespread violation of human rights and strongly condemns it. The imposition of unjust life and lengthy prison sentences and the confiscation of religious scholars’ property, shortly after the disgraceful remarks made by the US Secretary of State against clerics and prominent figures of the Shia world, demonstrate the Bahraini rulers’ alignment with the US establishment’s efforts to foment religious discord. Undoubtedly, holding show trials and using the judicial system as a cover for the collective punishment and harassment of clerics and ordinary Bahraini citizens can in no way conceal the inhumane nature of this action or its incompatibility with the fundamental principles and norms of human rights. The leveling of entirely baseless and unfounded accusations, including alleged links with Iran, as grounds for the criminal prosecution of Bahraini citizens and their collective sentencing to lengthy prison terms, is a clear indication of the Bahraini rulers’ abuse of the judiciary to suppress any rights advocacy. This, in turn, will undermine the credibility of Bahrain’s judicial system, render the issued verdicts null and void, and further erode the legitimacy and public acceptance of the ruling class in the country. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, while firmly rejecting the baseless allegations leveled against Iran, calls on the Bahraini rulers to end their repression of the people and religious scholars and to respect their human and civil rights in accordance with human rights standards and Islamic teachings. It also emphasizes that a policy of repression and intimidation can in no way prevent the people of Bahrain from pursuing their legitimate and rightful demands.

item.title: Iranian Pakistani Foreign Ministers hold talks in Islamabad
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi, who is in Islamabad to attend the meeting of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO), met with Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar on Monday afternoon. Araghchi thanked Pakistan for its warm hospitality and the successful organization of the 30th meeting of the ECO Council of Foreign Ministers, emphasizing the need to strengthen multilateral cooperation, enhance economic and trade interactions, and expand coordination among member states. The two foreign ministers exchanged views on developing and expanding bilateral relations in areas of mutual interest. Araghchi and Ishaq Dar also reviewed regional and international developments and discussed the latest diplomatic efforts aimed at safeguarding regional stability and security.

The foreign ministers thanked Pakistan for hosting the summit and successfully organizing its 30th session, emphasizing the need to strengthen multilateral cooperation, expand economic and trade relations, and promote greater convergence among member states. Araghchi, referring to the productive discussions at the summit, particularly on Palestine and the strong condemnation of the genocide in the occupied Palestinian territories, stressed the urgent need for the international community and Islamic countries to address the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and the West Bank. item.title: ECO foreign ministers back Iran’s initiative to end US-Israeli imposed war
item.description: The 30th Meeting of the Council of Ministers of Foreign Affairs of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) concluded in Islamabad with the adoption of a final declaration. In one of the paragraphs of the declaration, ECO member states expressed concern over the security situation in the region (due to the US and Israeli regime’s military aggression against Iran). They voiced support for Iran’s recent initiative aimed at bringing the imposed war to a complete and permanent end. Highlighting the importance of diplomatic engagement, they also expressed support for the good offices and mediation efforts of Pakistan and Qatar. The Islamic Republic of Iran recently, as part of its responsible approach to using diplomacy to end the imposed war, conveyed through mediators its two-day plan, which includes Iran’s seven demands and conditions, as well as practical solutions for establishing peace and stability in the region. ECO member states also underscored the Islamic Republic of Iran’s position as one of the founding members of the organization and emphasized its important role in effectively contributing to the advancement of the organization’s objectives.

item.title: Meeting held between Iranian Pakistani Foreign Ministry spokespersons in Islamabad
item.description: Esmail Baqaei, Spokesperson for the Iranian Foreign Ministry, who is accompanying the foreign minister at the ECO Council of Foreign Ministers meeting, held talks with his Pakistani counterpart, Sajjad Haider Khan, in Islamabad on Monday morning. During the meeting, the two sides highlighted the shared historical, civilizational, religious and cultural bonds between the two neighboring Muslim nations and stressed the importance of leveraging the two countries' strong relations and mutual trust to strengthen ties across various fields, including media and culture. The Iranian and Pakistani foreign ministry spokespersons also emphasized the importance of deepening mutual understanding and friendship between the two nations through media and underscored the need to establish appropriate mechanisms to enhance coordination on media-related issues.

item.title: ECO Foreign Ministers’ Council Meeting opens in Islamabad
item.description: The 30th session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) opened in Islamabad on Monday morning, November 16, under the chairmanship of Pakistan’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar, with the participation of foreign ministers from member states, including Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi. The meeting, attended by foreign ministers and senior diplomats from ECO member states, will discuss the organization’s efforts to expand economic, trade, transportation, energy, tourism and other forms of cooperation among its 10 member countries. Discussions will also cover agenda programs and ongoing initiatives aimed at strengthening ties among member states. The ECO Vision 2035 document, which seeks to outline the organization’s cooperation prospects over the next decade, will also be reviewed. In addition to representatives of member states, senior officials from several international and regional organizations are attending the meeting, including the Secretary-General of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), the Deputy Secretary-General of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO), and the Director General of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA). The ECO chairmanship will also be handed over from Kazakhstan to Pakistan at the summit. Pakistan will assume the organization's rotating chairmanship for a two-year term covering 2026–2027. The 30th session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) opened in Islamabad on Monday morning, November 16, under the chairmanship of Pakistan’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar, with the participation of foreign ministers from member states, including Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi. The meeting, attended by foreign ministers and senior diplomats from ECO member states, will discuss the organization’s efforts to expand economic, trade, transportation, energy, tourism and other forms of cooperation among its 10 member countries. Discussions will also cover agenda programs and ongoing initiatives aimed at strengthening ties among member states. The ECO Vision 2035 document, which seeks to outline the organization’s cooperation prospects over the next decade, will also be reviewed. In addition to representatives of member states, senior officials from several international and regional organizations are attending the meeting, including the Secretary-General of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), the Deputy Secretary-General of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO), and the Director General of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA). The ECO chairmanship will also be handed over from Kazakhstan to Pakistan at the summit. Pakistan will assume the organization's rotating chairmanship for a two-year term covering 2026–2027. The Islamic Republic of Iran is scheduled to host the 18th ECO Summit in Tehran in December this year.

item.title: 30th Meeting of the Council of Ministers of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO)
item.description:

Honorable Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan,
Distinguished Ministers and Heads of Delegation,
Honorable Secretary General,
At the outset, I wish to express my sincere appreciation to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan and the ECO Secretariat for convening this important meeting. I also extend my gratitude to His Excellency, my dear brother, Mr. Ishaq Dar, Honourable Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Pakistan, for his able leadership within ECO and the warm hospitality extended to my delegation. I also commend the Honourable Secretary General Mr. Asad Majeed Khan and his dedicated team. I would also like to extend my sincere appreciation to all those who, both at this meeting and on other occasions, have unequivocally condemned the acts of aggression against the territorial integrity of the Islamic Republic of Iran and its people, and have conveyed their heartfelt condolences and expressions of solidarity to the Government and people of Iran following the martyrdom of our esteemed Supreme Leader and the loss of other innocent lives as a result of this aggression.
Convening this meeting amid profound worldwide transformations and growing uncertainty underscores the imperative of advancing collective cooperation, strengthening coordination and convergence of our positions, and translating shared commitments into concrete actions within ECO.

Original source: https://en.mfa.gov.ir/portal/newsview/797775

بسم الله الرحمن الرحیم

Honorable Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan,

Distinguished Ministers and Heads of Delegation,

Honorable Secretary General,

At the outset, I wish to express my sincere appreciation to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan and the ECO Secretariat for convening this important meeting. I also extend my gratitude to His Excellency, my dear brother, Mr. Ishaq Dar, Honourable Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Pakistan, for his able leadership within ECO and the warm hospitality extended to my delegation. I also commend the Honourable Secretary General Mr. Asad Majeed Khan and his dedicated team. I would also like to extend my sincere appreciation to all those who, both at this meeting and on other occasions, have unequivocally condemned the acts of aggression against the territorial integrity of the Islamic Republic of Iran and its people, and have conveyed their heartfelt condolences and expressions of solidarity to the Government and people of Iran following the martyrdom of our esteemed Supreme Leader and the loss of other innocent lives as a result of this aggression.

Convening this meeting amid profound worldwide transformations and growing uncertainty underscores the imperative of advancing collective cooperation, strengthening coordination and convergence of our positions, and translating shared commitments into concrete actions within ECO.

Distinguished Colleagues,

Amid the ongoing transformation of the international system and global economic dynamics, ECO is moving beyond its traditional role towards becoming an effective platform for collective action, strengthened cooperation and joint efforts, enabling Member States to address emerging challenges and contribute to an inclusive and equitable global economic order.

In the current global and regional context, trade, transport and energy should constitute the three strategic pillars of ECO cooperation. Strengthening connectivity, facilitating intra-regional trade and enhancing energy cooperation will reinforce our collective resilience, mitigate external vulnerabilities and foster a more integrated and self-reliant region.

Iran welcomes the establishment of the Technical Negotiation Committee to reform ECO Trade Agreement (ECOTA). It is essential that current parties actively pursue negotiations to re-negotiate the Agreement, while encouraging other Member States to join the process. A modern, new-generation, more inclusive, effective and operational Trade Agreement can expand regional trade, strengthen economic resilience and protect our economies for the benefit of all people of the region.

Excellencies,

The Islamic Republic of Iran has consistently upheld international law, the Charter of the United Nations and the principle of peaceful settlement of disputes including through diplomacy. Over the past two years, Iran has remained committed to diplomatic engagement and peaceful solutions. Regrettably, the United States opted for an entirely different course, marked by aggression, threats, targeted assassinations, economic coercion, and blockades, in flagrant violation of international law and the UN Charter. These acts have resulted in the martyrdom of Iran's Supreme Leader and several senior political and military officials, as well as the brutal killing of more than 5,000 Iranian citizens, including 168 students and teachers at the Minab school. Therefore, the prevailing insecurity in the Persian Gulf and developments surrounding the Strait of Hormuz stem from the hostile policies and joint acts of aggression by the United States and the Zionist regime against Iran. This reality cannot be misrepresented.

The Islamic Republic of Iran has consistently sought friendly and constructive relations with its neighbours and has no inherent dispute with the regional countries. However, one principle speaks loud enough: the territories, airspace and facilities of the regional countries must not be used as platforms for launching attacks against each other. Iran's legitimate defensive measures are directed exclusively at the targets and military bases of the aggressors and should in no way be construed as actions against the peoples or governments of the neighbouring countries.

These circumstances highlight the urgent need for genuine, inclusive and regionally owned dialogue on security arrangements, particularly based on non-aggression and preventing any third party from using one country's territory or facilities to commit aggression against another.

The continued imposition of sanctions intended to deepen economic hardship and deprive the Iranian people of their fundamental rights has only strengthened their resolve to defend their legitimate rights and interests and resist excessive and unlawful demands. I sincerely appreciate the Member States that have demonstrated solidarity with the Iranian people during these challenging circumstances.

Given the growing impact of US and Israeli regime aggression on regional energy security, strengthening energy cooperation has become an urgent strategic imperative. Our region needs not only an independent security framework but also a reliable and sustainable regional energy mechanism to safeguard energy flows, ensure stable supplies, reduce external vulnerabilities and enhance collective resilience against geopolitical shocks and disruptions.

One of ECO's key priorities over the past year has been formulating its vision for the coming decade, following extensive meetings and consultations. Building on lessons from the implementation of the previous vision, this document emphasizes results-oriented approaches, practical implementation and measurable outcomes. It is therefore essential to implement it on the basis of directives and guidelines that would be instructed by our Leaders at the 18th ECO Summit in Tehran on 4 December 2026

Ladies and Gentlemen,

Before concluding, I deem it necessary to draw Your attention to the most pressing international crisis. It is imperative that this issue remain firmly on our collective agenda and that we do not allow it to fade into oblivion.

The situation in the Occupied Palestinian is a shame for humanity. It represents the gravest moral and humanitarian crises of our time, unfolding against the backdrop of the international community’s deeply regrettable inaction.

Over the past three years, Gaza has witnessed a full-scale genocide. The commission of atrocious war crimes and genocide, continued occupation, attempts to alter the demographic composition of the territory, the use of prohibited weapons, widespread destruction and devastation, forced displacement, and the obstruction of the entry of essential humanitarian supplies into Gaza constitute only part of the destructive and dangerous measures undertaken by the Israeli regime.

Alongside the terrible conditions in Gaza, we are witnessing the intensification of expansionist policies by the Israeli regime in the West Bank and occupied Al-Quds, including the unlawful expansion of settlements, daily terrorist attacks by extremist settlers against Palestinians, and the systematic displacement of the Palestinian population in the West Bank. Equally, we must not overlook the dire and deeply concerning plight of nearly 10,000 Palestinian held in Israeli regime prisons, where they are reportedly subjected to various forms of severe physical and psychological torture and ill-treatment.

Today, particularly amid the harsh winter conditions, Gaza urgently requires immediate and effective action to press the Israeli regime to lift the imposed humanitarian blockade and ensure the unimpeded entry of international humanitarian assistance, particularly food, medicines, temporary shelter facilities, and the materials necessary for the reconstruction of vital infrastructure. Such assistance is indispensable to addressing the urgent needs of more than 1.5 million displaced and homeless Palestinians.

The international community now faces a profound test of its commitment to humanitarian principles and responsibilities in addressing the humanitarian crisis in Gaza and the West Bank. This is a moment that calls for concrete action, collective responsibility, and an end to silence and indifference.

Dear Colleagues;

Building a more equitable and inclusive future requires deliberate action and collective commitment. We must ensure that our countries and region actively contribute to shaping the emerging international order and determining its future direction. The Islamic Republic of Iran firmly believes that its stability and prosperity are intrinsically linked to those of other ECO Member States. Guided by this conviction, Iran remains committed to promoting stronger, more effective and tangible cooperation within ECO.

I look forward to welcoming Your Excellencies to the 18th ECO Summit next month 4th December, in Tehran.

Thank you for your kind attention.

item.title: Iranian Foreign Minister to visit Pakistan Oman in coming fays
item.description: Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmail Baqaei announced that Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi will visit Islamabad and Oman in the coming days. The meeting will focus on discussing and exchanging views on economic and trade cooperation among the organization's 10 member states. The Foreign Ministry spokesperson also announced Araghchi's visit to Oman, saying that the foreign minister will travel to Muscat on Tuesday to meet and hold talks with his Omani counterpart.
